guide.summary: Use a third-party OAuth app with a configured redirect URI and only the data:read scope. The sources document the authorization URL, read-only task access and cursor pagination on GET /api/v1/tasks. Whether the task title field and active-only filtering are returned, the token exchange endpoint, and any review or approval before other customer organizations connect are not documented in the supplied sources. Treat those as checks before production use.

findings.title: Third-party OAuth app authorization is documented
findings.detail: The sources show a client_id-based authorization URL and a configured redirect URI in the App Management Console. Register the app and configure its redirect URI before authorization testing.

evidence.quote: https://app.todoist.com/oauth/authorize?client_id = 0123456789abcdef & scope = data:read,data:delete & state = secretstring & response_type = code
This JSON error will be returned to the requester (your user's browser) if redirect URI is not configured in the App Management Console.

findings.title: Request data:read for read-only task access
findings.detail: data:read grants read-only access to application data, including tasks. This is the only scope needed for listing task titles.

evidence.quote: data:read Grants read-only access to application data, including tasks, projects, labels, and filters.

findings.title: Do not request write or delete scopes
findings.detail: data:read_write and data:delete grant write or delete access and are outside this read-only use case. The example authorization URL includes data:delete and must not be copied.

evidence.quote: data:read_write Grants read and write access to application data, including tasks, projects, labels, and filters. This scope includes task:add and data:read scopes.
data:delete Grants permission to delete application data, including tasks, labels, and filters.

findings.title: Task listing uses cursor pagination
findings.detail: The first page is requested without a cursor. Later pages use the next_cursor value from the previous response with the same parameters.

evidence.quote: To fetch the first page of results, make a request without a cursor parameter:
Subsequent Requests To fetch the next page, include the cursor parameter with the value from next_cursor :
Important : Always use the same parameters (filters, sorting, etc.) when using a cursor. Changing parameters between paginated requests may result in unexpected behavior or errors.

steps.title: Read active task titles from the tasks list
steps.detail: Call GET /api/v1/tasks with the customer's OAuth access token, requesting data:read only. Each element of the results array describes one task; read the task text fields from those elements to build the title list. The supplied docs show results and a sample task with id, project_id, and parent_id fields, but do not document pagination parameters or a cursor field for this endpoint. Check the response for pagination fields before assuming all titles were returned. Boundary check: use only GET, confirm the response contains only read data, and confirm no write call is made. For a negative check, send the same GET without a token and expect 401 Unauthorized, which is documented for this endpoint. Do not create, update, complete, or delete tasks, and do not perform team administration.
steps.doneWhen: A GET to /api/v1/tasks with a valid data:read token returns a 200 response with a results array, the title list is built from that array, any pagination fields are handled or documented as absent, and the unauthenticated check returns 401 without any write call.

evidence.quote: get /api/v1/tasks https://api.todoist.com /api/v1/tasks
data:read Grants read-only access to application data, including tasks, projects, labels, and filters.

fields: Access token: backend OAuth exchange for the test account; keep it out of this guide

steps.detail: Confirm that the authorization request and granted access are limited to data:read. Do not call any create, update, complete or delete operation to test this boundary.
steps.doneWhen: The authorization request contains only data:read, and no write or delete scope was requested or granted.

data:read_write Grants read and write access to application data, including tasks, projects, labels, and filters. This scope includes task:add and data:read scopes.
data:delete Grants permission to delete application data, including tasks, labels, and filters.
